newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end lower for second day. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end lower for second day. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed slightly lower for the second straight day Tuesday as investors took profits and a break after last week's spirited, record-setting rise.
But the Nasdaq Composite index hit a new record high for the third session in a row, rising 11.16 points to 1,443.11, thanks to gains in technology stocks.
(Corrects final Nasdaq index finish).
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 0.53 of a point to 894.43, a new high.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 11.31 points at 7,760.78 after rebounding from a selloff of nearly 70 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,239 to 1,231 on heavy volume of 542 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The market was in a profit-taking mode despite new data that confirmed inflation was still dormant.

The government reported that the Consumer Price Index for May inched up 0.1 percent last month. Excluding the often-volatile food and energy components, the core CPI rose 0.2 percent, in line with Wall Street's forecasts.
"I think it is basically selling on the news," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "There is nothing to suggest it's inflationary and it's not a cause for concern."

The data showed that inflation remained in check, further strengthening Wall Street's belief that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates when it meets in early July. But the market still headed lower.
"Wall Street finally got the news and some just made a sale to hold on to their gains," said Jack Baker, senior managing director of trading at Furman Selz.
The benign data on retail prices came on the heels of a tame Producer Price Index last week.

"The CPI was the last nail in the coffin for the Fed -- the most important data between now and their July meeting. It looks like clear sailing ahead. The Dow could test 8,000 in the next few weeks," said Baker.
In another report, housing starts for May fell 4.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted rate of 1.397 million, compared with a revised rate of 1.468 million in April.
Although the Dow closed in slightly negative territory, analysts said its ability to overcome the early weakness was a sign of the continuing strength of the bull market.

"You still have a lot of people buying on dips, especially fund managers who need to show they were in the hot stocks before they send out their statements" at the end of the second quarter, said Charles Payne, analyst at Wall Street Strategies.
Traders said volatility could pick up ahead of Friday's "triple witching" expiration of options and futures.

Personal computers stocks were led higher by an upbeat outlook for the second quarter and bullish comments by Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc. on industry bellwether Compaq Computer Corp., whose stock rose 3-5/8 to 108-3/5.
Dell Computer surged 5-1/2 to a 52-week high of 120-7/8 after it said Monday that it was "very pleased" with its second-quarter results.

Reynolds & Reynolds Co. dropped about 22 percent after it forecast disappointing quarterly earnings. The provider of information management services fell 4-3/8 to 15-3/8 and was the most heavily traded stock on the NYSE.
Amgen Inc. slid 3-9/16 to 58-9/16 after said it expects it slower sales growth of its drug Epogen, which boosts the number of red blood cells.
Portugal's national electric company, Electricidade de Portugal, shot up 8-21/32 to 34-1/2 after its first day of U.S. trading.
The American Stock Exchange index was off 2.31 to 625.86.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.08 to 465.09. The average share was unchanged.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,434.431, up 14.578 or 0.17 percent.
